Subject: HealthBridge KMS/BYOK questions (transient custody + emergency rotation)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We circulated the updated RFI (attached) to the InfoSec and procurement teams and have a couple of follow-ups before we move to a vendor short‑list: 

1) Transient/delegated custody: our operations team needs to understand whether Redwood supports issuing short‑lived, scoped BYOK credentials to third‑party custodians (e.g., our HSM partner) for limited maintenance windows. If supported, what is the typical maximum TTL for those keys and how is scope enforced?

2) Emergency rotation SLA: in an incident where we need immediate key rotation (e.g., suspected compromise of a key-encrypting-key), what is Redwood’s guaranteed time-to-rotation for keys under BYOK? What manual steps are required on our side and what automation can you provide?

3) TLS profile and cipher compatibility: we need a definitive list of minimum TLS ciphers and TLS versions supported by Redwood Private endpoints behind a customer VPC. Please call out any ciphers that are disabled by default and whether customers can request changes.

4) Evidence: can you provide an operational runbook / excerpt that shows the emergency rotation flow and the audit trail entries we can expect (log IDs, retention windows)?

Attached: HealthBridge_KMS_RFI_v2.xlsx (annotated).

Appreciate a written response; we may request a short call to walk engineering through the specifics after your reply.

Best,
Megan Li

Megan —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and pointers; I’m copying Marissa (Customer Engineering) and Karthik (Product PM for KMS/BYOK) for technical detail and runbook artifacts. See also the attached excerpt from our public runbook (redwood_kms_runbook_v1.pdf) and a short Drive link.

Summary answers (high level):
1) Transient/delegated custody:
- Short‑lived credentials: supported via scoped wrapping tokens and limited service accounts. We support TTLs down to 15 minutes and up to 72 hours for scoped maintenance credentials by default.
- Scope enforcement: enforced at the request proxy layer and by token-scoped ACLs; operations only permit key import/export or key‑operation scopes explicitly granted. Audit entries are created for token issuance and every API call.

2) Emergency rotation SLA:
- Standard BYOK emergency rotation target: 4 hours from confirmation of a cryptographic incident for coordinated rotations when Redwood performs orchestration; 24 hours if the customer must perform the manual import of new key material.
- Steps from Redwood side: trigger revocation of active wrapping tokens, create replacement key variant, route traffic to fallback model variants, and run KV cache purge.
- Customer actions: if BYOK with customer-managed HSM keys, customer needs to import new wrapped key material within the agreed window; our portal will accept a signed import bundle.

3) TLS profile:
- Minimum supported TLS versions: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. TLS 1.1 and earlier are not supported.
- Default cipher suite policy: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 prioritized for TLS 1.3; ECDHE‑AESGCM suites for TLS 1.2 (e.g., ECDHE‑RSA‑AES128‑GCM‑SHA256).
- Disabled by default: CBC suites and RSA key‑exchange are disabled by default. Customers with explicit compliance needs can request a managed profile change via support ticket; changes require an approval and configuration window.

4) Runbook & logs:
- Runbook excerpt attached and shared at: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/KB-KMS-Runbook (see sections 4.2 emergency_rotation, 7.1 token_issuance).
- Audit trail: each rotation operation emits a RotationEvent (rotation_id), TokenIssue entries (token_id), and KeyMaterialChange logs. Logs are retained per our standard retention (13 months) and can be exported to a customer SIEM/CloudWatch for longer retention.

We’ll follow up with a short call to show the portal import flow and a demo of the emergency rotation path. Proposed times below.

Regards,

Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Mon 19 Jul 2027 10:30 AM PST works for our engineering team. I’ve set a provisional calendar invite and added an agenda: 1) emergency rotation end‑to‑end (10 min demo), 2) token issuance & scoped TTLs (10 min), 3) TLS profiles & custom profile request process (10 min), 4) Q&A and next steps (15 min).

On propagation: the 4‑hour target assumes coordinated orchestration within a single primary region and automated cross‑region propagation; for full multi‑region cutover we recommend a staged propagation plan — typically completes within 6–8 hours depending on traffic mirroring and cache TTLs. We’ll show the propagation dashboard in the demo.

Sample audit schema (quick):
- rotation_id: string (UUID)
- rotation_time_utc: ISO8601 timestamp
- changed_by: service_account or user id
- before_key_hash: base64 sha256
- after_key_hash: base64 sha256
- token_id: string
- request_origin: ip or service id

We’ll include an export example in the readout.
